title: IaC makes architecture repeatable
points: Template describes intended resources and dependencies
CloudFormation creates and updates stacks in one account/Region
Reuse across accounts/Regions needs deployment strategy and parameter differences
Elastic Beanstalk, Service Catalog and SAM can use CloudFormation underneath
diagram: Source template→validation→change set→regional stack; separate integration cards for Beanstalk, Service Catalog, SAM.
remember: A template is desired state; deployment is a controlled operation.

title: Read the stack before updating it
points: Review proposed Add, Modify, Remove and possible replacement
Change set preview does not guarantee success or complete property-level effects
Check resources with data, IAM changes and service quotas
Execute after approval and monitor stack events/rollback
diagram: Current template+proposed template→change set preview→approval→execute→events and verification.
remember: Preview replacements before they can destroy state.

title: DeletionPolicy protects the old resource
points: Delete default applies unless exception or explicit policy
Retain leaves resource and charges; Snapshot only for supported types
RDS DBCluster and standalone DBInstance default Snapshot
S3 bucket delete requires empty bucket
diagram: Resource removal branches Delete, Retain, Snapshot; separate replace path governed by UpdateReplacePolicy.
remember: DeletionPolicy does not protect a replaced physical resource.

title: Replacement requires a second policy
points: UpdateReplacePolicy controls the old physical resource on replacement
DeletionPolicy handles stack deletion/removal, not replacement
Choose Retain or Snapshot where supported for data-bearing resources
Test endpoint changes and restore before changing identity
diagram: Old DB v1→replacement v2; UpdateReplacePolicy controls old v1; stack deletion policy controls v2 later.
remember: Replacement and deletion are different events.

title: Custom resources extend a stack
points: Custom resource receives Create, Update and Delete requests
Lambda or another provider executes unsupported or external operations
Provider reports success/failure and stable physical ID
Handle timeout, retries, rollback and idempotent delete
diagram: CloudFormation→custom resource provider→external API or S3 cleanup→response to stack; failure/rollback branch.
remember: A custom resource can block a stack if it never responds.

title: StackSets deploy across accounts and Regions
points: Administrator defines StackSet and target instances
Self-managed needs administrator/execution roles; service-managed uses Organizations integration
Choose Regions, account/OU targets and operation preferences
A StackSet is regional even when it deploys to many Regions
diagram: Administration account StackSet→two account boxes each with Region instances; permission mode gate.
remember: A StackSet is not a globally self-healing stack.

title: Automatic OU enrollment has a boundary
points: Service-managed permissions can auto-deploy to new target OU accounts
Removal/move can trigger delete or retain behavior per configuration
New accounts use StackSet defaults, not prior overrides
Monitor failed instances, concurrency and failure tolerance
diagram: OU membership changes→StackSet automatic operation→new/removed stack instance; failure status route.
remember: Enrollment must be configured and monitored.

title: Drift compares template and actual state
points: Manual change can diverge from a template without automatic prevention
Detect stack or resource drift for supported types/properties
Review expected versus actual configuration and remediation safety
A successful stack status does not prove in-sync resources
diagram: Template expected SG source /32 versus live 0.0.0.0/0→drift report→controlled remediation.
remember: Drift detection observes; it does not itself block a manual change.

title: Secrets Manager references at deploy time
points: CloudFormation can reference a secret value without embedding it in template
Secrets Manager owns secret and rotation lifecycle
Runtime application/database integration must consume rotated value appropriately
Protect resolution permissions, logs and replacement-sensitive properties
diagram: Secret in Secrets Manager→dynamic reference resolution→RDS property; rotation path distinct from stack update.
remember: A rotated secret is not automatically a new CloudFormation deployment.

title: Import an existing resource safely
points: Manual import template describes whole stack and target resource
Provide resource identifier and DeletionPolicy for imported item
Import must not create/delete/change other resources in same operation
After import run drift detection; one resource cannot belong to two stacks in same Region
diagram: Existing S3 bucket+whole-stack template+identifier→IMPORT change set→managed stack→drift check.
remember: Import changes management ownership, not the resource identity.

title: Automatic import has narrower rules
points: Auto-import needs supported type with static custom name and identifier
DeletionPolicy must be Retain or RetainExceptOnCreate
Manual import accepts any valid DeletionPolicy for imported resource
Neither path should assume arbitrary resource types are supported
diagram: Two alternative import lanes with distinct prerequisites; converge on managed stack and drift check.
remember: Check import method prerequisites before writing the template.

title: Service Catalog separates admin and user
points: Admin authors versioned approved product and portfolio
IAM grants end users portfolio/product access
Launch constraint can use scoped provisioning role
User launches provisioned product with approved configuration
diagram: Admin→product version→portfolio+constraints→authorized user→provisioned product.
remember: Portal access and provisioning authority are distinct.

title: Constrain a self-service product
points: Product template or supported Terraform artifact is not the entire policy
Portfolio association, access and constraints shape allowed launches
Provisioning role scopes actual resource creation
Review tags, parameters, updates and termination behavior
diagram: Portfolio permissions and launch role both feed product launch; blocked branch for disallowed parameters.
remember: A catalog product can still be unsafe if its launch role is broad.

title: SAM is a CloudFormation transform
points: AWS::Serverless::Function, API and StateMachine simplify declarations
SAM CLI builds, packages, locally tests and deploys
CloudFormation operates transformed resources in the target stack
Local testing cannot prove cloud IAM/network/integration behavior
diagram: SAM template→transform/synthesized CloudFormation resources→stack; local test loop separate.
remember: SAM reduces boilerplate; CloudFormation remains the deployment engine.

title: SAM traffic shifting uses aliases
points: Publish Lambda version and route via alias
DeploymentPreference configures CodeDeploy gradual shift
Pre/post traffic hooks and alarms can support rollback
Verify end-to-end API and data compatibility during shift
diagram: CodePipeline→build/test→SAM/CloudFormation→CodeDeploy shifts alias v1→v2→API; alarm rollback path.
remember: A traffic shift needs measurable rollback conditions.

title: CDK synthesizes before deployment
points: TypeScript, Python, Java, C# and other supported languages define constructs
cdk synth outputs CloudFormation template and assets
Bootstrap resources/permissions can be needed for deployment
Review synthesized IAM and replacement effects, not only source code
diagram: CDK app→construct tree→synth template/assets→CloudFormation→AWS resources.
remember: CDK code is not directly executed by CloudFormation.

title: Choose CloudFormation, SAM or CDK
points: CloudFormation templates directly express resources
SAM adds serverless syntax and local developer tooling
CDK uses programming constructs and synthesizes templates
All need review, guardrails and deployment roles
diagram: Three alternative authoring cards converge on CloudFormation stack; Service Catalog is separate self-service distribution.
remember: Pick authoring experience independently from governance.

title: Validate policy before execution
points: Schema/lint and tests catch template mistakes
CloudFormation Guard checks JSON/YAML against policy rules
Hooks can warn or fail stack operations when configured
Config drift/evaluation runs after deployment and serves another question
diagram: Source→lint/Guard→change set→Hook policy gate→stack→Config drift/evaluation; distinguish stages.
remember: A local Guard check is not an enforced deployment gate unless wired in.

title: Guard rules express desired properties
points: Require S3 encryption and disallow open SSH in templates
Test rules on both compliant and noncompliant fixtures
Run validation in build and preserve output with deployment revision
Rule coverage depends on paths/properties and exceptions modeled
diagram: Two small YAML-like resource examples→Guard PASS/FAIL→build decision.
remember: An untested policy can reject good stacks or miss bad ones.

title: Hooks enforce at the stack boundary
points: Hook target/action/filter controls where validation runs
Warn mode records issue; fail mode blocks operation
Guard, Lambda, custom and Control Tower controls can back hooks
Account/Region activation and service permissions affect coverage
diagram: Change set execution→configured Hook evaluates→warn or fail→resource operation only if permitted.
remember: A Hook must be activated and scoped to the intended target.

title: Separate design, deployment and runtime roles
points: Author can edit code without production deployment authority
Deployment role needs scoped CloudFormation and passed service role
Service role creates supported resources; custom Lambda has its own role
Protect IAM/PassRole, KMS, S3 assets and termination actions
diagram: Author→pipeline→CloudFormation execution role→resource APIs; custom provider separate.
remember: Least privilege has multiple roles, not one administrator.

title: Walkthrough: safe RDS template update
points: Inspect change set for replacement and data impact
Apply UpdateReplacePolicy/Snapshot as appropriate
Approve during maintenance with backup/restore plan
Deploy and validate endpoint, data and stack events
diagram: DB v1 template→change-set replacement gate→snapshot/retention→DB v2→health/data validation; failure rollback.
remember: Do not treat a successful template validation as a safe database replacement.

title: Walkthrough: import a live S3 bucket
points: Capture bucket name and current configuration
Build full stack template with target bucket and DeletionPolicy
Create IMPORT change set without unrelated create/update
Execute then detect drift and reconcile differences
diagram: Existing bucket→template identifier+policy→import change set→stack ownership→drift report.
remember: Import first; alter configuration in a later reviewed update.

title: Walkthrough: block an unsafe security group
points: Proposed template opens SSH to 0.0.0.0/0
Guard rule fails validation before change set
Hook in fail mode can enforce in deployment
Correct source CIDR, rerun policy and inspect stack events
diagram: Unsafe template→Guard FAIL; corrected template→Guard PASS→change set→Hook→stack.
remember: A passing check has meaning only for rules actually configured.

title: Policy controls act at different boundaries
points: CDK Aspects inspect or alter the construct tree during synthesis
Guard evaluates templates or change sets where configured
CloudFormation Hooks can warn or block stack operations
SCPs bound principal permissions across an organization; Config detects deployed state
diagram: Four parallel layers: CDK synth, Guard/Hook deployment validation, Organizations SCP permission boundary, Config postdeployment evaluation. Do not draw as a single mandatory chain.
remember: Choose a control by the boundary it actually enforces.

title: Secrets in IaC: reference, rotate, consume
points: Secrets Manager dynamic references and Systems Manager secure parameters avoid plaintext template values
CloudFormation resolves supported references during stack operations
A rotation event does not automatically update a stack or every consumer
KMS and IAM permissions, logging and consumer refresh require separate design
diagram: Two alternative secret stores feed CloudFormation resolution at deploy; distinct runtime consumer and rotation paths; no automatic stack update arrow from rotation.
remember: Avoid plaintext and verify how the application receives a rotated value.
